utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning to everyone in and around this courtroom. Madam Registrar, would you please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is the case IT-03-69-T, The Prosecutor versus Jovica Stanisic and Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Registrar. If there are no procedural matters to be raised, I would like to -- Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: There's just one which I think will hopefully put Your Honours' mind at rest a little. The protocol has been agreed so there is no need for a court hearing tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That is a good message, but agreed between NFI, Mr. Brown, and Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So agreement, a three-party agreement. I'm really relieved. And if I was perhaps a bit -- if I seemed to be slightly irritated that was done on purpose to urge further progress to be made.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: More than understandable.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Your Honour, a piece of information that Mr. Jordash may not have. The examination is scheduled for the 31st of October to the 11th of November.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me see. The examination, Mr. Groome, is that when Mr. Brown --

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Brown has requested that from the NFI. The Prosecution took no position on the scheduling of the duration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Examination -- I was thinking about examination of witnesses but it is the examination of the documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Of that diary. That is -- which means that Dr. Brown, then, or Mr. Brown, would need how much time then to prepare his report?

utterances.speaker: MR. GROOME
utterances.text: Not to speak for Mr. Jordash, but Mr. Brown in a conference call yesterday said about two weeks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Two weeks. So then the Chamber now will seriously consider to extend the time-limit until the 1st of December. Yes, this kind of procedural information is very welcome. Could the witness be escorted into the courtroom. And are we in private session or closed session, or are we in open session?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I saw on the screens that the outside world might have thought that we were not in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Just in terms of one housekeeping matter. Yesterday, at the end of the session, the witness was -- did produce the notes, and we did make a copy, and we have the notes available here in the court available to return to the the Court Usher to give back to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think can be returned right away to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Novakovic. Mr. Novakovic, the usher just returned to you the small note you gave yesterday to the Prosecution. Mr. Novakovic, I would like to remind you that you're still bound by the solemn declaration that you've given at the beginning of your testimony on Tuesday. That is, that you will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber will now continue his cross-examination. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Novakovic.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, today could you please listen carefully to my questions and direct respond to what is being asked of you. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The head of the Uzice DB between 1990 and 2000 was Jakov Sokic; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Sokic is now deceased; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: As part of your duties, did you ever go to Prizren in southern Kosovo prior to 1996?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What was your assignment there?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My assignment there was, again, to work on counter-intelligence tasks, and I also went to assist there in Prizren in their centre, because the situation had become more complex, security-wise, and they needed assistance.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If you could give us approximate date of this assignment.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can tell you approximately. I went sometime in November 1987, and I spent there the entire year of 1988, and then I returned to the Uzice centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it your testimony, then, that you were never assigned to that location in 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In 1995? In that location? No, I was never again in Kosovo after that. The last time was in 1988, and I returned from there in December.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you receive any increases in your salary between the 10th of July and 10th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An increase in salary? I can't remember now. It's too long ago. When I was on field missions, I received per diem.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you recall if you received any per diem between the 10th of July and 10th of August, 1995?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I received per diem in November 1995. Yes, I did receive per diem in November 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: So the record is clear: You did not -- is it your testimony that you did not receive, then, a per diem between -- or in July or August of 1995.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I cannot tell you exactly. It was 17 years ago.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: During your assignment to the Uzice sector, did you have access to information reports of other administrations and other sectors?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a more seasoned employee, I did receive surveys and overviews from other areas. Or perhaps people from other centres came to be briefed on the situation in Uzice. I would learn from them about the problems in -- in their localities, especially if they were relevant to the work of our centre. In the counter-intelligence field.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: On Tuesday, you stated that you were transferred to the 2nd Administration in Belgrade in November 1995. Were you ever assigned to Sremska Mitrovica as a permanent employee between 1996 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was never assigned to Mitrovica, but that area that I went to sometime was directly across from Mitrovica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You reported and received directions from Franko Simatovic between 1994 and 1999; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it was from November 1995 to 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Simatovic is your former supervisor in the 2nd Administration; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, who in the State Security Service had access to all information and reports from all administrations and sectors?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, ex officio, the chief of the service would have access. He needed to be informed. Otherwise, I did not have access to material from other administrations, except if there was something of common interest, something that we needed to jointly work together on. The chief of administration had access to all the documents created by that administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: When you refer to chief of service, I take it you're referring to Jovica Stanisic. Could you please confirm that and tell us the name of the person that you're referring to as the chief of administration?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I said that somebody had access to all the materials of the service, that would be only the chief of the service. But when I say chief of administration, I mean the senior chief, the head of that administration.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you to provide the names of those two individuals so that it's clear for the record.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, as an example, I can tell you the chief of the service was Jovica Stanisic at the time --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir --

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I was just going to suggest that my learned friend gives a time-frame.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Four hours. Four hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think that Mr. Jordash was asking you to giving a time-frame for the witness. To answer the question when --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because you asked for names. I think the witness first referred to functional description. But if you ask for names, then you need persons during a certain time-frame to be on that post.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Fair enough.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, this case relates to a specifically charged time-period between 1991 and 1995. I'm asking you who had access to all information and materials from all administrations and sectors during that time-period. If you could please provide us the names.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, from what I remember at the time, people changed in both the position of chief of service and chiefs of administrations. So if you're asking me specifically about 1995, the chief of service was Jovica Stanisic; the chief of the 2nd Administrations was Franko Simatovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did those two individuals have access to all information and reports from all administrations and sectors? Sir, if you could please focus on my question, it is quite specific.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Franko Simatovic as chief of the 2nd Administration had access to the documents created in the 2nd Administrations or centres that were under the 2nd Administration in terms of their intelligence line of work. Franko Simatovic [as interpreted] had access to all the documents, but, of course, he is not going to burden himself with all the documents. He is going to be briefed by chiefs of sections about things he needs to know. He didn't have time to look through all the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 8, line 2, the name that was written is not the name that was said. The paragraph refers to another person, not the one named in line 2, page 8. That's what I heard in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I do not see any name in the second line of page 8. Oh, yes, I see that my neighbour to my left has a -- oh. Yes. What is -- what is page 8, line 2 for me is -- line 1 for me is line 2 for others. That comes as a bit of a surprise in the system. But let me try to clarify this. You told us that Franko Simatovic, as the chief of the 2nd Administration had access to the documents created in that administration or centres, or that were -- I think sent to or up to the 2nd Administration in terms of their intelligence line of work. Now, you then said and you mentioned a person that a person had access to all the documents but, of course, he is not going to burden himself with all the documents. What name did you mention there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I mentioned the chief of service ex officio, Jovica Stanisic. Ex officio, he had access to all the documents, but, of course, he was presented with selected documents by chiefs of administrations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So what you said is that Jovica Stanisic had access to all the documents but, of course, he was not going to burden himself with all these documents and he is going to be briefed by the chiefs of sections. That's what your testimony is? Yes. No, it was transcribed and translated to us in a different way so that has been clarified now. Please proceed, Mr. Weber. Thank you, Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Throughout your entire time in the Serbian DB, the principle of secrecy applied to all activities undertaken by you and your colleagues; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Throughout my work, the main principle in the work of the service was the principle of conspiracy, subordination, and rationality and professionalism. Those were the four main principles that were absolutely observed in the work of the service.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I would like to change topics with you now and talk about a little geography. There were three border crossings points in the Uzice sector between Bosnia and Serbia. If you could confirm these points for me. These crossings were along the Drina river at Mokra Gora on the road from Visegrad to Uzice. A second point at Uva on the road from Rudo to Priboj, and the third one being located between Bajina Basta and Skelani; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is it correct that the Serbian MUP was responsible for controlling all three of these crossings points?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Serbian MUP was in charge of crossings.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Were you aware of paramilitary units that were present in the area of Skelani and Bajina Basta in 1992, through your employment?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard they were present, but I did not have direct insight into that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mount Tara is located within the area of responsibility of the Uzice DB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Serbian DB used facilities at Tara; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know that in one period they used.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: You are aware of the JATD; correct? A simple yes or no is fine at this time. It is something that we'll discuss further.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Members of the JATD wore red berets and were known by others as such; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, JATD was JATD. But others were -- called it the Red Berets. It was an anti-terrorist unit, but some people called them the Red Berets because they wore red berets.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Milan Radonjic was one of the deputy commanders of the JATD; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about that. Possibly. I can't be sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1D5061 shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this is a Serbian DB JATD proposal for awards dated 9 May 1996. Did you along with Zoran Rajic and Dragoslav Krsmanovic receive pistols as awards for service in the JATD?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This document, I suppose, is authentic. But I've never been in the service of the JATD. In my whole career, I never served the JATD. But it's true that I was rewarded that year with a pistol, probably at the proposal of some of the leaders of JATD for my service in Krajina.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, could you please give us a brief explanation as to the reason that you did not mention any knowledge of the JATD during the topics that were discussed with you in the last two days?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because nobody asked me about it at any point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time the Prosecution tenders 1D5061 into evidence. It was received by the Prosecution from the Republic of Serbia pursuant to a RFA. It is one of many documents that came from a personnel file of Dragoslav Krsmanovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objections. Madam Registrar, the number would be ...

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be P3018, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence under seal, Mr. Weber of ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, based on the content in this exhibit and the fact that Serbia did not provide it with any redactions, we would submit that it is not necessary to be under seal. However, if the Chamber would like to take a cautious approach on that, that would be fine too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: There's no present member of any intelligence service mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, so I can give you 100 per cent certainty on that, if I could please have just the next break and I will check on one name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Provisionally under seal. But, then, of course, it may have been shown to the public. That should be provisionally be redacted. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, when did you first hear of Operation Tomson?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard of it sometime in 1994 or 1995, perhaps. That operation was conducted by the 3rd Administration that was in charge in encountering, extremism and terrorism. In Uzice we mainly followed the guide-lines of that operation from the beginning of war operations in Bosnia and Herzegovina, due to the fact that Uzice is in the border-line territory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Individuals or groups who were not considered a security threat would not be included in Operation Tomson; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. Both individuals and groups who were considered a security threat were subject of surveillance under Operation Tomson.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have D428, marked for identification. This is formally 65 ter 1D392. This document is provisionally under seal, and we request that it not be broadcast to the public. It is a lengthy document, and we have seen that the witness does like to have hard copies, so we do have a hard copy of the exhibit to be presented to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could the usher assist.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, before you is the 19 September 1995 Uzice State Security Department report on the results of Operative Action Tomson. Could you please confirm whether you reviewed this report in its entirety prior to your testimony in this case?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I reviewed the document in its entirety. The Defence provided me with the document to peruse. I had not had an occasion to see it beforehand, but I did have an occasion to see it when the Defence provided it to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: According to your comments in the Defence chart, is it correct that you considered this report a "high quality analysis by the Uzice centre dealing with both Muslim and Serb extremism."

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. I thought that this material was of a very high quality because it did not adopt a selective approach to the arming of various groups. It, rather, represents a cross-section of the work of the Uzice centre dealing with both Muslim and Serbian extremism. This is a collective overview of all the things that were done, what arms were seized, what measures were undertaken, what about the co-operation with the Ministry of Interior with this regard. This material even lists somewhere, but I'm not sure where, that all the documents that the Uzice centre dispatched with this regard did not contain the wording "Operative Action Tomson" in the heading. However, in its work, the Uzice centre absolutely complied with everything that was defined by the Operative Action Tomson. The Uzice centre behaved in that way. In 1992, 1993, and 1994, and this is an overview leading up to 1995 and spilling even over that period.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to go through this report with you in more detail.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: If the Prosecution could please have page 2 of the B/C/S and English versions of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And, sir, if you could please keep your answers as precise as possible to the questions that I'm putting to. First, the Prosecution would like to discuss with you the groups that were considered extremists by the Serbian DB according to this report. The second paragraph of the introductory remark states: "Tectonic political shifts within the FRY, in particular the introduction of a multi-party parliamentary system, provided an incentive in space for reactionary, extremist nationalist and separatist forces to appear on the political stage. Enveloping their extremism in the shroud of legal political parties these forces displayed extreme hostility and intolerance towards other parties, in particular the ruling one. Unable to reach their political goals through normal and regular parliamentary procedures, some of these parties resorted to other means, primarily military ones of achieving their goals. They set up groups and organisations with the overtones and characteristics of paramilitary formations, which, at a given moment could be used as a framework for the unconstitutional, illegal, or rather, unlawful overthrow of the actual authorities." My first question to you: Is it correct that Operation Tomson was directed at disarming paramilitary formations that were politically opposed to the ruling party in Serbia and could potentially overthrow the authorities in power, including Slobodan Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The primary goal of the Operative Action Tomson was to control and disarm individuals and groups that either returned from the front line or were supplied with weapons in a different way, in order to provide security for the territory of Serbia. Inter alia, the arming of such groups for the reasons that you, yourself, spelled out could have threatened the constitutional order of the Republic of Serbia, i.e., it could have threatened the authorities in power at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, what I just read to you doesn't discuss all groups. It addresses particularly ones that may pose a threat to the ruling party and the authorities in power. Is that correct that that's what that section states?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says. But the sentence goes on and explains what the whole thing was all about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm going to go through this document with you in greater detail. If we could please go section at a time and we'll discuss the different groups.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, if the witness is asked a question about a certain section where he considers that read in isolation it gives a wrong impression, he is entitled to include a reference to other parts in his answer. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Could the Prosecution actually please have e-court page 5 of the B/C/S original and page 3, middle of the page, of the English translation of this document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. In my copy -- oh, well, no, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, at the end of the remarks. Directing your attention to the last paragraph of the introductory remarks which is before you on the monitor. This paragraph begins: "Illegal arming organised by parties and paramilitary forces organised by Muslim extremists and cessationists in the area of Raska and the Republic of Montenegro, under the aegis of the SDA constituted a special security problem in the Republic of Serbia and the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia in the past period and still partially does." Sir, nothing in this sentence that I just read to you indicates that the Serbian DB was concerned about the crimes being committed by Serbs against Muslims or Croats outside of the borders of Serbia; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct this concerns the years 1992, 1993, and 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The --

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I'm reading the correct page. I -- I think it's page 4, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you are, the paragraph before you continues to state that: "Successful actions carried out by the MUP of Serbia and Montenegro in 1992, 1993, and 1994 have resolved most of the problem, and legal sanctions were used to bring into custody the participants and organisers." My question to you on that is: Is it correct that the Serbian DB considered Operation Tomson a successful means of disarming Muslim extremists and paramilitary formations who were politically opposed to those in power?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Operative Action Tomson was an operative action conducted by the state security sector of Serbia. And it applied exclusively to the territory of Serbia. Muslim terrorists was -- were just one of the groups of terrorists. And in that passage, it is stated that Muslim extremists were a security threat and the threat for the constitutional order of Serbia, amongst all the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, page 16, line 22, an organisation is mentioned, or there is a record of the organisation in the transcript that I didn't hear the witness mention at all.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic I will read the beginning of your last answer and I invite you to then repeat what you said after the words I read to you. You said, "Operative Action Tomson was an operative action conducted by...," by whom?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] By the state security sector of Serbia with all of its organisations and centres in the territory of Serbia. And not in the territory of --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I continue to read: "And it applied exclusively to the ..." And then you said? Did you say the territory of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The territory of Serbia. What I meant by that was armed groups, illegally armed groups, paramilitaries.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I think that the matter has been the -- The translation and the transcription gave us a different impression but it has now been corrected. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have e-court page 10 of the B/c/S original and page 6 of the English translation of this report.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, for your information this is the page with the number ending in 9931 in the lower right-hand corner. I would like to look at some examples of how Operation Tomson was implemented by the Serbian DB between 1992 and 1995. I will then have some further questions for you. This report details the seizure of weapons, ammunition and other equipment from a group of nine Muslims in October 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For the record, Your Honours, I believe there is a typographical error in the date on the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The report indicates that criminal reports were filed against every one of these individuals. Do you know where the Serbian DB initiated criminal proceedings with the public prosecutor's office against all of these individuals who were considered Muslim extremists?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The only thing I can say is what I see in the document. That's all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Which is?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Which is that in October 1993, based on operative work and intelligence gathered, we know that the group of Muslims from Prijepolje was in possession of illegal arms that they had obtained with the help of individuals of -- with the help of individuals of Serbia ethnicity. The state security sector searched several houses and other facilities in Brodarevo in Gracanica and Prijepolje villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: What is the reason that the State Security Service would consider important to initiate criminal proceedings against all nine of these individuals, based on what you just said?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know what? Illegal possession of arms and the arms were found on them. Ammunition and other equipment. That was a good enough reason to instigate proceedings which consisted of checks, seizure of illegal -- illegally possessed weapons, and further legal measures that could be applied in such cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have e-court page 18 of the B/C/S original and page 11 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, this the page number ending in 9939 in the lower right-hand corner. This report continues to detail the seizure of weapons from 49 individuals in 1994 who are associated with the White Eagles, a Serbian military extremist group. According to this document, criminal reports were only issue against nine of these individuals?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: For the record this information can be found on e-court page 19 of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you know why the Serbian DB initiated proceedings against some of the White Eagles and the majority were released after being issued a weapons receipt and providing a statement?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was customary in the work of the service and, to be very specific, that was one of the most radical groups in the territory of Priboj and in the territory of our centre so it was customary for such individuals that weapons be seized from them, that they be prosecuted, and the rest of the individuals would continue to be monitored by the service and would be subject to other types of procedures applied by the state security sector. And this example speaks about the non-selectivity and the equal measures being applied to all extremists found in the territory of our centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Are you saying that you don't find any selectivity in the fact that the Serbian DB decided to initiate criminal proceedings against only nine of the 49 individuals, and with respect to the remainder, let them go after receiving a weapons receipt and taking a statement? Isn't that selective treatment?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that you will found -- find a comment here regarding all the measures that were applied against those individuals. In addition to the illegal possession of arms that were seized, it says that criminal reports were filed, that they were interviewed, that the weapons were seized from them, and that a large majority of the cases were then transferred onto the authority of the state security and that all the information was transferred to them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, fine. We will go -- let's go through a specific example then and then we can come back to this. The Prosecution would like to direct your attention to the White Eagle named --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I apologise. Page 20, line 11, the -- the authority of a different sector, not the one that is indicated in here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Witness, I'll read part of your answer. Could you please then repeat what the following part of your answer was. You said arms were seized. It says that criminal reports were filed, that they were interviewed, that the weapons were seized from them, and that a large majority of the cases were then transferred to the authority of ... What organisation or institution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] To the public security sector. The authority of the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that all information was transferred to them. Yes. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, the document doesn't reflect that that's the case, so I'd like to go through a specific example so we can deal with details. The Prosecution would like to direct your attention to the White Eagle named Milomir Djurovic who is listed on number 28 on e-court page 24 of the B/C/S and page 15 of the English translation. If we could please have those pages on the screen. Sir, this is it on page 9945 in the lower right-hand corner of the hard copy in front of you. Sir, could you please review this information for Mr. Djurovic only and let us know if prior to your testimony you were provider with a 3rd Administration report related to this seizure?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I receive or was I provided with a report here? I didn't understand what you -- you're asking me. What report? And who I was provided report from?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm happy to explain, sir. With respect to the person listed at number 28, Mr. Djurovic, did the Defence provide with you a 3rd Administration report related to this seizure?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely not. This is a collective document and that was what was provided to me by the Defence. This is how I'm looking at it, and based on what I see, I provide my comments to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Is your knowledge then limited to the document that was provided by the Defence?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I provided comments to the documents that were provided to me by the Defence for my perusal. As for my knowledge, I can say that this is a summary report provided by the analytical department of the Uzice centre. This is a collective overview of all the tasks accomplished pursuant to Operation Tomson. I understand your specific example. However, when you look at the list containing the names of 49 individuals, that list ends with the concrete taxative enumeration of what was done, how many reports were filed, how many interviews were taken, what would follow, what procedures would be undertaken, and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you, sir.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have 65 ter 1D1024 shown to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This is the Uzice DB 3rd Administration report dated 8 April 1994 on the possession of illegal weapons by Milomir Djurovic. The second paragraph of this report states, quote --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. I do not know if there are any restrictions to this Defence document. I did ask that it not be broadcast.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I -- I -- I would just need a moment to have a look to see if there's any material falling within Your Honours' order.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could we provisionally not show it to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The second paragraph of this report states: "In return for occasional repair work on a car while he was at the front in Dobrun, 1992, Zoran Bojovic gave Djurovic a Schmeizer submachine-gun and a semi-automatic rifle. Later, Djurovic gave the submachine-gun to Dragan Papic of Priboj, and on Bojovic's order he gave the semi-automatic rifle to Mr. Dragoje Zvizdic." The sentence indicates that the semi-automatic rifle wound up in the possession of Dragoje Zvizdic. Do you know why Mr. Zvizdic was not included as one of the 49 White Eagles listed in the 1995 Tomson report we have been looking at?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You're asking me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, I'm asking if you know why he wasn't included in the report?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Why Zoran Bojovic didn't making it to the report?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: No, sir. Why the person who wound up in possession of the weapon, Mr. Zvizdic -- he is not referenced in the report. There's no need to look at it. Do you know why he wouldn't make it into that report?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think. I suppose that he was subject of further operative work. I have no doubts that the service continued dealing with him. Maybe he was not available to the service at the time, but I'm sure that the service continued working on his identification.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Okay. At the end of this report, the document provides the personal details of Dragoje Zvizdic and indicates that he is unemployed. The Serbian DB had the ability to check these personal details at the time the report was compiled, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It certainly had, but I'm telling you again, in that period, a certain number persons and a certain number of measures were handled but we were concentrated then on -- on routes of arms smuggling and supply, because that's the time when people went to war in other areas. They were from the area of Priboj but at that time they were active in the area of Bosnia. I don't know why he wasn't included in the report, but he was certainly included in our surveillance measures, in our operative measures.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: This report does not indicate that the Serbian DB even issued a receipt or obtained a statement from Mr. Zvizdic. Do you know why the Serbian DB would not have undertaken either of these measures?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was probably not accessible to them. I don't know the reason.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P2896 for the witness. The exhibit is presently under seal and we ask that it not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: While that's coming up, Your Honour, I think there's a name of the operative on the previous exhibit --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And therefore should not be shown to the public and to the extent it has been, a video redaction should be made. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Thank you to the Stanisic Defence for that information. With that information, we tender the document under seal, at this time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: No objection. Madam Registrar, the number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: The number would be P3019, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And is admitted into evidence under seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, this is a MUP Republic of Serbia certificate for Dragoje Zvizdic dated 15 March 1994 for performing tasks on behalf of the MUP. The certificate is issued by Milan Radonjic the same person who signed you're award proposal. Did you know that Mr. Zvizdic was a member of the JATD in 1994?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know anyone under that name.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours. My learned friend is asking the witness whether he knows that Zvizdic was a member of the JATD. Nothing in this document indicates that. It says a member of the serve force of the MUP. I don't see from this that this person, if it is the same person, is defined as a member of the JATD. I think one should be fair to the witness when putting questions of this kind.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I noticed that as well, Mr. Petrovic. Whether it's fair or unfair to the witness may depend on other documentation to follow. I think the comment would have been appropriate at a later stage, once we would have dealt with the subject matter. Mr. Weber, any follow-up on the specific assignment you just put to the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, there is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Therefore under those circumstances, Mr. Petrovic, you should have allowed Mr. Weber to continue. I noticed it as well, but you were a bit early with your comments. Please proceed, Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did you know whether or not Mr. Zvizdic was a member of the JATD or even a reserve unit of the MUP of Serbia in 1994?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, have you listened to the last answer of the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I see the last answer. Thank you, Your Honour. I'm sorry I missed it with the [Overlapping speakers] Mr. Petrovic. That's my fault.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Putting questions one but listening to the answers is also a very relevant part of cross-examination. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if someone was actually employed by the MUP of Serbia, would that explain the reason that they would not be included as part of Operation Tomson?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yesterday, it was mentioned that there was a possibility for the service to use sources or to use as sources people who were close to the subjects we had a security interest in, but it happened rather rarely that we would be interested in a member of the reserve force of the MUP. But we did look for our sources in the environment where activities took place that were relevant to us. I have no idea whether the operative in charge or the centre in charge knew that Zvizdic was on the reserve force of the Ministry of Interior.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Could the Prosecution please have Exhibit P1512, page 5 of the B/C/S and English versions. The Prosecution requests that this exhibit not be broadcast to the public.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Before you, sir, is a JATD payment list of daily allowances provided by the Serbian DB in the first half of April 1994. This is the same time in which the report that I showed you earlier was from. This list is similar to the per diem list, D429, which you commented on in the Defence chart that includes your name. The individuals on this list include Raja Bozovic, Davor Subotic and Mr. Zvizdic among others. Is it correct that members of certain special units such as the JATD were not included as part of Operation Tomson because these individuals had a relationship with the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You say these persons were covered by Operation Tomson? I can't understand that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm actually asking you. These persons were not covered by Operation Tomson because they were associated with the Serbian DB. They received payments from them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Perhaps, Mr. Weber, is your real question whether, if a name pops up in Operation Tomson of a person who is the member of the JATD that no further action would be taken against that person. Is that ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Tomson reports that we have been provided, for example, the one that we looked at with the witness, does not include any of these names. So our position and my question would be [Overlapping speakers] intentionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In the reporting in Operation Tomson, that if, during the operation, it would come across a person who is a member of the JATD, that that person would not be included in the Tomson report. That's the issue.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no idea of whether those people ever cropped up, because I had nothing to do with the JATD then. I had nothing to do, no contact with the newly established unit. The only contact I had was in the area of Krajina in November 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The JATD was never considered an extremist group; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The JATD was a unit established by decision of the Ministry of Interior, as far as I know. It was not an extremist group.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Returning more generally to the topic of the White Eagles, the Prosecution possesses 3rd Administration reports that describe the exceptions and activities of the White Eagles as early as April 1992. Do you know why the Serbian DB did not undertake actions to disarm this group in 1992 and, instead, waited until 1994?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me tell you, the way the RDB worked was when they got some initial information they would develop it further with the application of further operative measures in order to be able to get to the subject and process them. Rumours about the subjects in the -- the territory of Croatia, Bosnia didn't mean anything to us, and that's why I still have a reservation regarding these people. They might have been processed later either by us or by the public security sector. I don't know, in fact, what kind of activities you are talking about.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Would it be important to act immediately if you were concerned with the safety of Muslims? Wouldn't it be important to act in a timely manner and not wait and collect information, if that was your concern?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was a specific danger to a specific Muslim person or a specific group of Muslims, of course it would have been important to act immediately. No doubt about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, at this time, the Prosecution seeks to bar table four documents to show information possessed by the Serbian DB about the White Eagles in 1992. These documents are 65 ter 6263 to 6266. The documents are Uzice DB 3rd Administration reports dated 24 April, 4 June, 27 August, and 5 October 1992. The Prosecution is offering these documents to show the information that was known to the Serbian DB in 1992 and failed to act upon until 1994. All of these documents were received by the Office of the Prosecutor pursuant to official requests for assistance 1695 from the Republic of Serbia on 15 September 2008. These documents originate from the BIA archives. The Prosecution made a copy of this RFA available to the Defence and I know one was provided to the Simatovic Defence in particular prior to this examination. The documents are being offered at this time due to the evidence being offered by the Defence in relation to Operation Tomson which did not derive originally from the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I'm -- first of all, could I just raise the issue of I'm not sure where the Prosecution obtains the conclusion that the DB didn't take action. It's been presented as fact, but with no corresponding exhibit or testimony referred to. So I think that -- that might be useful if we knew where Mr. Weber derives that conclusion before it's presented as fact. In relation to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, facts, of course, it's a position taken by the Prosecution, which is, of course, not accepted for its factual accuracy. What I do understand is that, Mr. Weber, with this witness, went through operational activity in 1994 has put to the witness that information was available already in 1992. Of course, whether 1994 was the first action taken or not, that may be the position of the Prosecution, but that's, of course, still to be considered.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: It was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Your argument is totally valid. That, if you point at an action taken in 1994 that that does not mean, in itself, that no action was taken in 1993, and I can imagine that would be an argument by the Defence. But at this moment we are just focussing, I think, on documentary evidence which would demonstrate what kind of information was available in 1992. I think that's the limited purpose of what Mr. Weber seeks to establish.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Whatever conclusions he may have on his mind, Mr. Jordash, might not be the conclusions you would have on your mind, and what the conclusions of the Chamber will be, will become clear at the end of this case.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: In relation to the application to add documents through the bar table, we'd oppose that application. I think where we have got to relates to Your Honours' guidance on the admission into evidence of documents tendered by the Prosecution during the Defence case, the decision dated 26 August 2011, which allows the Prosecution to use documents with a witness in order to elicit evidence. The first step, we would submit, that the Prosecution must do is to use the evidence to elicit evidence in favour of their case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: One second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered the matter, Mr. Jordash, not exactly in line with what you argued but also not exactly in line of what Mr. Weber asked. Mr. Weber did put to the witness that the OTP has material that shows that information was already known in 1992. The witness then is -- in his answer, not knowing what that material was. Said something about rumours, well, we -- of course then you would have to investigate and it could well be that at a later stage. The Chamber considers it appropriate that the witness, first of all, will be provided with those four reports so that the witness who apparently was not familiar with the details of the information available about the White Eagles in 1992 has an opportunity to read that material and then to see whether what he suggested in his answer, whether there's a good ground for that, for example, if it would just be rumours, that would be a -- and then we'll then decide once the witness has had an opportunity to look at it, to comment on it, whether or not it's appropriate to admit those documents into evidence. That is what the Chamber is inclined to do, and I'm looking to both of you, and I -- no one is stamping with his feet on the ground, so apparently -- Mr. Weber, were you willing --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: That's fine, Your Honour. The Prosecution proceeding the way it did just to -- trying to make efficient use of the time [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I think we could use the break for that. We are at a point for a break anyhow. And perhaps if the Chamber could briefly look at that material so that we could better understand the -- the possible comments the witness may have after the break.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour. If the Prosecution could just have a couple of minutes to go upstairs to get clean copies. We only have marked copies with us in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then I think it's time for a break. Mr. Novakovic, we have some work for you to be done during the break. You may have noticed that the Prosecution referred to information which was available in 1992 about the White Eagles and you were not familiar with that information. You'll get the four reports, and you'll have an opportunity to answer questions and to comment on those reports, especially in view of the action taken in 1994, because that's the focus of Mr. Weber, his questioning. Would you be so kind to read through those four documents. You will receive them once they are copied. And could the Chamber have English translations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Of course, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then we take a break, and we resume at ten minutes to 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, did you have an opportunity to read the documents? Did you receive them and did you read them? Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber may have some questions or may invite you to comment. Mr. Weber.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, over the recess, you were provided with four reports from the 3rd Administration of the Uzice DB in 1992. Do these reports reflect information that the DB centre had in 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Did one of these reports, 65 ter 6263, dated 24 April 1992, include a poem that was a part of a leaflet which expressed the intent of the White Eagles in June of 1992 -- I'm sorry, excuse me, in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Directing your attention to the hard copy of 65 ter 6264 that's in front of you, it's the report dated 4 June 1992. In this report, it states: "The White Eagles basic activities boiled down to slaughtering and killing of the Muslims." Does this information indicate that the Uzice DB was aware of these activities. As can you see from this document that you indicated dated 4 June 1992, those were members of the White Eagles from the areas of Obrenovac and Valjevo and it was written by the Uzice centre without indicating specific names and surnames who was in charge.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you allow me to explain, all the four documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if you could provide a general comment on them that's fine. On the four documents.

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: All these four documents say that, at the time, the Uzice centre was working to identify occurrences of hostile nature like the work of various organisations. The first document dated 4 June mentions Zoran Penezic from Priboj and this amalgamated material indicates that a criminal complaint was filed against him later. This is initial information. When the war in Bosnia just began and when they first came to the attention of our centre. It took a lot of meticulous work to identify and find out about the work of this individual.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, sir. I know I invited you to give a global comment on all four. But because you are mentioning something here, when you say Zoran Penezic, is it correct that he was not arrested until later in 1994, in the Tomson report that you were referring to, the criminal report?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Precisely. But because he had a weapon him, monitoring the work of political parties was not commonly accepted in Serbia by the society. The multi-party system was just emerging and what the political parties did not manage to achieve in parliament, they tried to pursue by creating military wings and paramilitary unit. But it's obvious that they focussed their activity on propaganda under the territory of Serbia. But the other activities were pursued by paramilitary formations in the war in Bosnia. From this information, you can see that initially they were identified as potential vehicles of hostile activity in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, and you can see that from the first document among the four. He was processed either by the seizure of his weapons or via concrete forms of work. I would like to emphasise that amalgamated material --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, if I -- I know that there --

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honours, at this time, the Prosecution -- the document speaks for themselves and the witness is repeating what the documents are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let's try to -- to cut matters short.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: First of all, when you talk about the first document, you say the document of the 4th of June, I see the first document dated 24th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe Your Honour is referring to 6264, the 65 ter documented 4 June 1992?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. I don't have 65 ter numbers here. I see one document dated the 24th of April, Uzice DB State Security Department Centre. Extremism, Official Note of the employees of the RDB. That's the first -- in chronology, that's the first one I see. Now, I think, second -- let me try to -- in response to one of the questions put to you by Mr. Weber, more or less saying why nothing was done, that was the gist of that question, you said these people had arms. Is it correctly understood that if persons affiliated with political parties and carrying arms that if information was known about them, that the fact that they were carrying arms and that they were linked to a political movement or party, that that would be a reason not to intervene? And I'm talking about 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely. That was sufficient reason to react, if we established they had weapons and you can see that from this material. But if they were not armed on the territory, and they pursued propaganda activities, it was not easy to just start processing them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Let me then be very clear to you. Then I do not understand your answer saying, Well, they had weapons and it was not customary to proceed against political people. That's what your answer was. And in view of this answer, I have great difficulties in fully understanding your previous answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, then, I was misunderstood. That's not what I meant at any point. Illegal possession of weapons, regardless of what political party they belonged, would be subject to prosecution. The person would be brought in, interviewed, and the charges would be filed against him, according to the Law on Criminal Procedure, and then he would -- then he would be processed further by the public security sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Apart from what happened in 1994, could you give us an indication of arrests of any of the persons mentioned here in 1992 and/or 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From what I see from these four documents, Penezic was arrested and he was processed from this materiel. He was tried, Zoran Penezic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: When was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say. I don't know. I wasn't dealing with these cases myself but I can see from the documents he was prosecuted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: My question clearly was about 1992 and 1993 because that is the issue apparently raised by Mr. Weber whether and why no effective action was taken in 1992, where certain information was available and why action, and then not complete but only limited, was taken in 1994. That's the matter Mr. Weber is raising with you. Do you have any further -- apart from what you told us until now, do you have any further comment on that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The documents contain references to 1992, 1993, and 1994. And there is a list of actions that were taken, at what time, against whom, what was undertaken, and what was then transferred onto the authority of the public security sector. If you look at the document, if you read it, will you see it. There are individual names and the names of individual activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you for this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I believe there is some source of confusion occurring since the witness has one additional material in front of him right now which is the Tomson report which indicates the individuals were arrested in 1994.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. That was relatively clear to me. And the witness was not able to give any further details about the date. And so the only thing we have, as far as the date is concerned, we have before us is this 1994 date. Now, one additional question. You told us about propaganda but, of course, if people would have arms it would be quite different. Now, in the 4th of June 1992 report, it reads that the activities boiled down to slaughtering and killing of Muslims. Was any action taken, to your knowledge, at that point in time, in relation to this information? And --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is about crimes in the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina, not in the territory of Serbia. At that time, we had information about crimes in the territory of Visegrad of the so-called Visegrad theatre of war. However, judging by the information no reference is made to any individuals. There's just an indication that those persons are from Obrenovac and Valjevo. In the Uzice centre we didn't have anything to do with Obrenovac and Valjevo. Those places belonged to the authority of a different centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Nevertheless, the Uzice centre was right to report about it, so that they had nothing to do with it is, to some extent, contradicted by you reporting on it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] But there where no names. The report was drafted and sent to the headquarters in Belgrade, to the headquarters of the 3rd Administration who --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I see that. Do you know enough knowledge about any investigation trying to identify those persons by their names? I'm not asking whether you did it, but whether you know of any such activity, to try to find out who it exactly were that had committed such crimes. If you know tell us; if you don't know say, Well, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that the Uzice centre worked on the issues surrounding Sjeverin and Strbac. And as for the others that others investigate, I don't know. I didn't deal with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Weber please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Mr. Novakovic, I will come back a little bit to Visegrad in 1992 in a little bit. But before I do that, I'd like to change the topic completely. Yesterday at transcript page 14004, you stated: "The Presidency of the Republic of Serbia made a decision that special police units, the PJM, would be paid in this way, in per diem. In fact, they received salaries in their original units when they were employed but when they would go into the field, on field missions, to areas where security was disrupted. They would be paid in the form of per diem in keeping with that decision of the Republic of Serbia or, rather, its Presidency." Sir, are you talking about Slobodan Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time President Milosevic was at the head of the Presidency of Serbia. I said that I was not a financial expert, but I'm reading this in the document that this was the way per diems were paid.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Do you acknowledge that Milosevic authorised the payment of state security officials for their activities outside the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You can see from the decision that all the employees dispatched on missions out -- outside of the headquarters, or actually, the main office of the security office, primarily in the territory of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, are you stating -- I just would like be to clear with you, if we could. Are you saying that President Milosevic authorised, by decision, the payment of state security officials outside the Republic of Serbia, including Croatia and Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Petrovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would kindly ask the Prosecutor to show the witness the document. On page 14004, in the heading there's something that is very important for the witness's answer. It doesn't say the president of Serbia but the Presidency of Serbia. I'm going to deal with that in my additional questions, but this is of the utmost importance, and the witness should be shown the document in order to be able to answer appropriately.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, are you putting these questions to the witness because you think that the witness would have any direct knowledge of the involvement of President Milosevic in the preparation and/or the signing of that decision? That's my first question to you. Or would you -- or are you seeking him to draw conclusions from the fact that if there was a presidential decree, decision, whatever it is, that given the date of that decision that was at the time when Mr. Milosevic was president of Serbia? I mean, what -- what of the two matters are you raising?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the Prosecution does not agree with the Simatovic Defence [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... I was asking you a question, Mr. Weber. It's fine that you want to respond to Mr. Petrovic, but I put a question to you. Is it the first issue that you are raising with the witness or is it the second issue you're raising with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It relates to his personal knowledge and with respect to the document that the witness is being shown, but I'm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then apparently have you not understood my question. Do you think this witness, and we could ask him, has any knowledge of the role of Mr. Milosevic in this decision, direct observation? I know that he did this or did that. Or is it that you expect the witness to make deductions from the fact that at a certain date there is a presidential decision and that because Mr. Milosevic was the president at the time that, therefore, it must have been from Mr. Milosevic. Which of the two?

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It's the first, and it's based on his own knowledge that he expressed yesterday during the testimony. It is why I sought to confirm --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay, then please ask him very specific questions about this.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, yesterday you were shown your own per diem with your payment on it and you made a comment on that which I just read to you which does not reflect the content of that per diem fully. I'm asking you, that based on what you said, that the Presidency of the Republic of Serbia made a decision that special police units would be paid by per diems, whether it's correct or do you acknowledge that Milosevic authorised payment of state security officials for activities outside of the Republic of Serbia

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Please switch off unnecessary microphones. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] What I can say with full responsibility having seen the document, this is my comment to the document and the way per diems were paid, and this is what I see in the document. According to that document, the Presidency of Serbia made a decision on paying special police units. At that time the state security sector was part of the Ministry of the Interior. And the only legal way for our employees, for the employees of the state security to be paid when going outside was for them to be paid pursuant to the decision of the Presidency of Serbia. Whether Mr. Milosevic was directly responsible for that or not, I don't know. In any case the Presidency of the Serbia was the body that issued and drafted the document that I have just commented upon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: And the last part that you said, this fund that paid the salaries for those outside, or per diems for those outside Serbia who were deployed out there, that is your understanding of how that was done while you were in the State Security Service; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that I was paid in that way, me and my colleagues who went with me. We received per diems. The financial official of our centre, from Uzice where I worked, took the money from the 8th Administration of the headquarters in Belgrade. I suppose that the 8th Administration acted pursuant to the decision of the Presidency of Serbia for the payment of special police units, given the fact that the state security sector was part of the Ministry of Interior of Serbia. The document which shows the names of my two colleagues and mine also shows that the official of the financial sector of my service took the money from Belgrade from the 8th Administration, that, at the time, was involved in the logistics issue, and the issues of payment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Was the fund that was used to pay these per diems also spent on weapons, ammunition, and equipment for the special anti-terrorist forces of the Serbian DB, such as the JATD?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't have a clue, really. I'm not a financial expert to know how things were done.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I put it to you that you have knowledge about the JATD, that you have seen this organisation, and that you're aware that they were armed and were provided equipment by the Serbian DB; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the unit was established pursuant to a decision by the Ministry of the Interior as part of the state security sector. I assume that the ministry also armed it, i.e., that the sector armed it, not any third -- other, third party. I only assume, as I say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, you were a member of the 2nd Administration for a while. Are you aware that funds were allocated through the Presidency of Serbia for weapons and ammunitions of the special units of the Serbian DB?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Jordash.

utterances.speaker: MR. JORDASH
utterances.text: I think the witness has answered the question and said he --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, half yes, half no. Let's hear the answer of the witness. There is a constant confusion about funds, funding, arming. Of course, you would expect that if you arm someone that you fund that arming as well but that is not entirely clear and has been mixed up in some of the previous questions. So, therefore, Mr. Weber, unless Mr. Petrovic has something important to raise, I would allow the witness to -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PETROVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, with your leave, the question is not clear, given the difference constitutional or legal status of the categories that are mentioned. The Presidency of Serbia is one category, the president is another category, and the witness has to be clear in that. Things existed at different times and the witness may be aware of that or may not be aware of that. In any case, the question is not very precise or clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll hear from him. I don't think that this relatively long comment on the question was appropriate. But, Mr. Weber, could you also keeping in mind the time, the timing of -- of the events, could you perhaps rephrase your question so that any ambiguity is taken out of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm asking you about the JATD, which formerly existed between 1993 and 1996. I'm asking you specifically, based on your employment with the State Security Service, whether you were aware that funds were allocated by the Serbian DB, I'll be specific to that, for paying for their weapons and ammunition?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Absolutely. As far as I am concerned, absolutely. That wasn't within my purview. I was not in a position to know that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Then perhaps let's -- let's keep matters short. Let's forget about funds. I think earlier one of your answers was - and let me check that very precisely - you said: I know that the unit, talking about the JATD, was established pursuant to a decision by the Ministry of Interior as part of the state security sector. I assume that the ministry also armed it, that the sector armed it, not any third party. Do I understand your testimony to be that equipment, arms for this unit, were provided by the Ministry of Interior as part of the state security sector and that you are not aware of any outside funding of it, funding by a third party?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Precisely so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If it was set up by the ministry, I assumed that was the case. As I also said, I'm not familiar with the logistics of how things were done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Weber, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I just want to get back to the central issue that I originally asked you about which was about a fund used for per diems. Do you know whether this fund was also used for ammunition and weapons, the fund that was used for per diems?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That question has been asked and that question has been answered. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: I'd like to return to Visegrad in -- in the early 1990s. In 1991, is it correct that about 63 per cent of the population of Visegrad was of Muslim ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I wouldn't know that. I am not familiar with that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, have you tried to reach agreement with the Defence on what -- if you're referring to 1991, most likely you're referring to the census all well documented.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Happy to discuss this with the Defence over the next break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Why would we ask the witness about percentages if there is full documentation about the census in 1991.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: At the beginning of 1992, there were increasing tensions between the Muslim and Serbian population of Visegrad; correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: The Uzice Corps occupied the municipality of Visegrad from the 14th of April until they withdrew on the 19th of May [Realtime transcript read in error "April"], 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADENKO NOVAKOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure about the date, but I suppose you are right. In any case, it was either before war started or as soon after the war started. But in any case, it was the Uzice Corps that was responsible for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Weber, just to verify the transcript, did you never to the 19th of May or ...

utterances.speaker: MR. WEBER
utterances.text: It was the 19th of May.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
